messages:
sara: FYI we just got an urgent escalation from Acme Payments — their webhook consumers started receiving invalid JSON from our /v1/chat/stream endpoint after last night's model promotion. customer says parsers started failing and they had to pause ingestion.

sara: Repro notes they sent identical prompts to old model and new model; old -> clean JSON, new -> truncated object + stray commas. Happening only in streaming mode.

sara: sample curl they ran:
```
curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-4b","mode":"json","prompt":"generate_invoice({\\\"id\\\":\\\"1001\\\"})"}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/stream 
```

sara: response snippets (customer captured):
```
data: {"invoice": {"id":"1001","items":[{"name":"x","qty":1}],}
data: [DONE]
```

sara: They also saw a sudden spike in 5xxs and client retries which led to billing spike; they provided x-request-id: acme-req-20260301-7a2f

priya: Thanks — assigning to eng-runtime and eng-ml. Do we know if this aligns with last night's canary swap (model alias promotion at 02:14 UTC)?

tomas: Yes that canary promoted redwood-chat-4b:2026-03-01 -> stable at ~02:14. I'm pulling logs now. Can you attach the upload of their full trace?

sara: Uploaded logs to the ticket (link) and pasted their minimal repro above. They said errors started immediately after promotion.

kevin: Quick status: I see elevated latency and chunk boundary errors in the runtime around 02:14-02:22 UTC for a subset of requests to the streaming router. Some shards returned early eos tokens and left a trailing comma in streaming JSON assembly.

kevin: snippet from runtime log (masked):
```
[02:16:03] stream_chunk_flush shard=5 request=acme-req-20260301-7a2f status=partial_flush tokens=134 last_token=','
[02:16:03] stream_end_emitted shard=5 request=acme-req-20260301-7a2f reason=eos
```

maya: interesting — eng-ml pushed a quantized variant in the canary (4b-q8) to improve perf. Could be tokenization/decoder change that touches how streaming escapes are emitted.

priya: Priority = P1 for customer impact. Suggested immediate mitigation: (A) switch Acme to non-streaming (polling) endpoint, (B) pin them to previous model tag if possible, (C) hotfix runtime to ensure chunk-assembly never leaves trailing punctuation before final flush.

tomas: I can roll back the model alias for accounts with legal hold. Need customer org id to pin.

sara: Org id ACME-7765 provided in ticket. They requested rollback rather than changing client.

kevin: For rollback: we can promote redwood-chat-3b:20260228-stable back as alias for that org only via routing policy -> model_overrides. I'll prepare the canary rollback playbook steps.

maya: Root-cause hypothesis: quantized decoder emitted an extra phantom token when using short sequence flush path. That token was ',' which combined with our streaming JSON assembly produced an invalid trailing comma before the final closing brace.

kevin: Also noticed repeated 401s for some retries — gateway logs show an intermittent Authorization header rewrite when requests pass through edge D (edge-d-3). That caused some client SDKs to re-auth and retry, compounding the billing spike.

priya: So two related issues: streaming chunking bug + auth header passthrough on edge-d-3. We should treat as two fixes but coordinated rollback may be fastest for customer.

tomas: Action items I will take now:
- promote per-org model_override for ACME-7765 -> redwood-chat-3b:20260228-stable
- open rollback PR to revert global alias if others report regressions
- disable edge-d-3 auth-hotpath until we patch rewrite rule

kevin: Eng-runtime will add a safety patch to the streaming assembler: if flush occurs while partial buffer ends with ',' or trailing punctuation, buffer should stash sentinel and ensure final JSON is valid (no trailing commas). I'll raise a short-lived feature flag to roll quickly.

maya: Eng-ML will run targeted reproducer with q8 variant and short sequence flush path to validate. I'll push a failing unit test that simulates chunk boundary token = ','

sara: Customer requested ETA. Can we do per-org rollback in next 30 minutes?

tomas: I'll start the model_override now — ETA ~12m with validation. Will notify when done.

eng-bot: deployment: model_override ACME-7765 -> redwood-chat-3b:20260228-stable started by tomas at 1768511400

kevin: Patch diff is small, will try to get runtime flag out in next 45m, but rollback should unblock customer faster.

sara: Thanks team. I'll tell Acme we're rolling them back and we have a follow-up plan (patch + canary re-run + longer soak). Also will ask them to provide their client parser tolerances.

priya: After rollback, we should run a batch of their recorded prompts against new q8 variant with streaming enabled and check for trailing punctuation. Add an integration test to prevent future regressions.

tomas: Completed model_override for ACME-7765 at 1768512000. Customer confirmed parsing restored. Closing P1 after verification unless further errors reported.

sara: Acme confirmed payloads valid again and billing spike subsided. Leaving ticket open until runtime patch lands. :thumbsup:
